runners_data.name: Tachos
runners_data.note: Consistent performer for D K Weld who wants a prominent pitch and has solid Good-going form (11 from 15 on similar ground); five-year-old at OR 78, this is a winnable mark but needs to hold a position in a congested early-race scenario with 22 runners.

runners_data.name: Blues Emperor
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who comes here on a seven-day turnaround and has been placed on Good going before; trainer W Harvey has just one runner in the past 14 days, and this seven-year-old's blinkered form figures (6-4-8) suggest inconsistency — needs the race to fall apart late.

runners_data.name: Summer Snow
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up operator for Peter Lawlor who has found 1m on Good ground the right trip twice in recent history; McGettigan (5) takes the ride and the horse returns seven days after its last run — needs a clear passage in the straight that may be hard to find in 22 runners.

runners_data.name: Therewillbeglory
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's four-year-old has placed four times in five Good or heavy-ground runs at this trip and looks tailor-made for a prominent role; Ben Coen in the saddle is a significant plus, and the visored gelding's record of four seconds in five starts tells you it gets to the line but may need things to go right positionally.

runners_data.name: Banner Beauty
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who won on Good ground at 8f and has been running in the top half of the field in recent starts; the horse's last five runs on Good going produce a mixed record (5 from 7 placing) but the last two finishes (10th, 6th) suggest she is below peak form at OR 75.

runners_data.name: Brewing
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose stamina-grade form is mainly on softer tracks — only three placings from 15 Good-ground runs is a concern; Dylan Browne McMonagle is an elite booking but the horse is 38 days fresh and its recent form figures on fast surfaces are weak.

runners_data.name: Thyer
runners_data.note: 236-day absence is a significant flag — Maurice Ahern runs the horse fresh but this is a long lay-off; the five-year-old's two wins and six places on Good turf give some confidence in the going, but the fitness question in a 22-runner field makes it very risky from a hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Calm The Jets
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish, which is a real concern for a prominent runner who will be racing into a headwind of traffic; Rory Cleary takes over and the four-year-old has been beaten in both recent 8f Good-ground starts — its one win came on Soft and over a mile, so the form is fragile here.

runners_data.name: Chester Nimitz
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who won on Good ground at 6f and has placed four times in 11 Good-ground starts; Nicola Burns (5) riding from a prominent position with OR 73 makes this a mid-handicap player, but recent form figures of 7-0-1-5-9 are inconsistent for a horse expected to sit handy.

runners_data.name: Highbury See See
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's second runner and a consistent prominent type whose six recent runs at 8f on Good going produce steady mid-field to placed finishes; Seamie Heffernan is a major positive and the horse's record of two places in 15 Good-ground starts at this trip suggests competitiveness without certainty.

runners_data.name: Prevalence
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners the highest-rated horse in the field at OR 82, a three-year-old from the powerful G M Lyons yard whose trainer is 5 from 14 in the past 14 days; only two Good-ground runs from four outings (2 from 4 placing) but Keane's ability to find a run in a big field is a key asset.

runners_data.name: Spanish Rising
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's four-year-old has finished 0 from 4 on Good ground and is stepping down from 10-12f trips; Adam Grant (7) rides and the horse's two best efforts came at a mile-and-a-half or more — the drop in trip and consistent hold-up style make it a tough assignment in this traffic.

runners_data.name: Majestic King
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy rides this five-year-old who is tagged as fading in the finish and carries a prominent-racing profile — a dangerous combination; he has won and placed at OR 70 on Good ground at this trip, and Murphy may try to make the most of an early position before the fade sets in.

runners_data.name: Neo Smart
runners_data.note: Jim Bolger's five-year-old is a consistent prominent type who stays the mile trip well on Good ground (8 from 15 on similar going); Declan McDonogh is an experienced navigator in big fields and the horse's record of two places in 15 Good-ground runs suggests it will be there or thereabouts without necessarily winning.

runners_data.name: No More Porter
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race — Adrian McGuinness's eight-year-old has led and placed at 3-6 from four Good-ground starts; Adam Caffrey has no pressure from the field early and with 22 runners bunching behind him, the leader gets a potentially uncontested daylight advantage that makes him dangerous at OR 67.

runners_data.name: Usuario Amigo
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse on its best form, but the field contains more such types than the map can accommodate and it is likely to race further forward than ideal; the five-year-old has one win from 15 Good-ground starts and Kennedy (5) will need to adapt tactics — the style-fit discount is real here.

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's four-year-old is a true hold-up type whose form at 8f on Good ground is modest (6 from 11 placing), but it is mapped to midfield because the field is saturated with rear-division horses; Chris Hayes takes over and the horse's finishing efforts have been weak in recent starts, making it hard to fancy even if it gets the run of the race.

runners_data.name: Nautic Star
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides this lightly-raced three-year-old from Mrs John Harrington's yard, who has placed at 7f on Soft and ran second at 7f on Soft — stepping up to 8f on Good is a step into the unknown; only one from three runs on Good turf but Foley's tactical intelligence gives the horse every chance.

runners_data.name: Tofino
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by style, but Cromwell's four-year-old is mapped to midfield because too many horses are competing for that position; Jack Kearney (3) rides the horse which has placed four times in 15 Good-ground starts — its best form is on softer surfaces and it may not get the handy berth it needs.

runners_data.name: Albion Power
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose form on Good turf is limited (3 from 15 placing) and whose last five finishes (9-4-8-9-11) show no obvious improvement; Luke McAteer rides and the horse is racing in a position (mapped midfield) that is not its natural home — even from the right position, the form does not inspire.

runners_data.name: Liberation Date
runners_data.note: Jack Foley's three-year-old won at 7f on Soft and has placed at 7f on Soft twice — stepping to 8f on Good on a 33-day break is a step up in both trip and going demands; W J Lee is a reliable jockey in big fields but the horse's natural prominent profile will be tested in a 22-runner scramble for position.

runners_data.name: Chapel Lane
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan rides this three-year-old for W McCreery who is 1 from 15 in the past 14 days — trainer form is worth noting; the horse's style is unclear (U) but all four recent runs on Good going show place efforts and it carries a visor, suggesting it can be trusted to run its race even if its tactical position is unpredictable.

races.paceDynamic: No More Porter is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 22, and with a sustainable Good-ground pace expected over a mile at the Curragh, he is likely to dictate comfortably without being seriously pressured for the lead. However, behind him there is significant congestion: nine runners — including Tachos, Therewillbeglory, Calm The Jets, Chester Nimitz, Highbury See See, Majestic King, Neo Smart, Nautic Star, and Liberation Date — all want prominent positions, meaning traffic jams and interference between the two-furlong and three-furlong markers are a genuine danger. This field holds more prominent/front-running types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly; of those, Tachos, Therewillbeglory, and Highbury See See look most likely to secure the positions directly behind No More Porter given their draw and natural tactical speed. A controlled, single-paced mile on Good turf at the Curragh historically suits runners who sit handy in the first few behind the leader and travel well into the straight — the prominent-to-midfield profile that arrives with cover and a clear passage at the two-furlong pole is the standout beneficiary of this race shape.

watchPoints.text: No More Porter (front-runner) stealing a march on 22 rivals — if the prominent pack's congestion delays their response, Adam Caffrey could be many lengths clear before the field organises.

Prominent runners Tachos, Therewillbeglory, and Highbury See See are all converging on the same three to four positions behind the leader — a bump or check between the 2f and 3f marker could end the chances of multiple fancied horses simultaneously.

Prevalence (Colin Keane, OR 82, G M Lyons) is the highest-rated runner and dropping back in class — Keane's ability to thread through a 22-runner field from a hold-up position in the straight is the key variable to monitor.

runners_data.name: Tolebi
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping back up to 7f from sprint distances; Nicola Burns (5lb claim) is a positive, but sim-going record of 0W1P from eight Good-ground runs is a red flag, and the drop back from 8-runner fields to this 18-runner context creates traffic risk.

runners_data.name: Dar Toungi
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up performer dropping sharply in trip from 10f-plus distances to 7f for the first time in recent form; sim-going record (0W0P in 15 Good-ground runs) is deeply concerning, and 34 days off under a trainer out of form (T14: 2/6) compounds the worry.

runners_data.name: Arryaaf
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent type with an excellent sim-going record (1W3P from four Good-ground runs) and a Curragh win over 7f last season; the 231-day absence is the chief concern, but Michael Costa has hit a purple patch (T14: 1/14) and Luke McAteer keeps the ride.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing hold-up type who has been running over 8f on Standside ground; stepping back to 7f on turf Good could suit in theory, but sim-going figures (0W2P from 15) and 84 days off since a Standside campaign suggest a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Indigo Dream
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with three places from eight Good-ground starts; Colin Keane takes over and he has placed twice over 7f on Standard and Good ground — the eight in his last run was over 7f Good at the Curragh and is worth looking past, as he was better the two runs before.

runners_data.name: Spacebound
runners_data.note: Front-rank type who is unplaced in only one of three career starts, both places coming over 7f and 8f — goes fresh well (LR 62d); sim-going record is thin (1 run on Good, unplaced) but trainer Daniel McLoughlin is in form (T14: 2/12).

runners_data.name: Collecting Coin
runners_data.note: Prominent type (cheekpieces) with a Curragh win over 7f and further placed efforts; sim-going record of 1W3P from nine Good-ground starts is the best of the prominent group — Shane Foley retains and the 12-day turnaround following a reasonable run is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Gypsy Queen
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old prominent type off 376 days — the absence is the dominant concern, though she won on Good ground at the Curragh over 6f last season; the step to 7f is unproven and she requires a clean reappearance to feature.

runners_data.name: Little Empire
runners_data.note: Prominent type with placed efforts over 7f on Good ground (2/15 Good-ground record: 1W1P); the apprentice claim (Patrick McGettigan 5lb) is a marginal positive in a big field, and he has been in consistent if not spectacular form over this trip.

runners_data.name: Spodo Komodo
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent type resuming after 271 days — he ran on Good ground placing once (3/8f/GOO) and won on Soft; the layoff and step up to 7f from recent 6f and 8f outings make him speculative, though John James Feane's small string makes the appearance meaningful.

runners_data.name: Invincible Will
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type (hood) with OR 87 — the highest in the field — and won over 7f on Good at the Curragh; Jack Kearney's 3lb claim is useful in an 18-runner field and his trainer Gavin Cromwell is in rich form (T14: 6/45). Best-credentialled true closer in the race.

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner wearing a tongue-tie and cheekpieces; Chris Hayes knows the job and Denis Gerard Hogan's yard is firing (T14: 3/20). His Good-ground sim record (1W3P from 14 runs) is acceptable and he has placed over today's course at shorter — the key question is whether a solo lead is soft enough to hold on.

runners_data.name: Um Wadi
runners_data.note: Hold-up type (tongue-tie) from the Joseph O'Brien yard, which is in strong form (T14: 11/64) — that trainer angle is the most compelling reason to include him. His recent form over 7f on STA and Good shows a place at 7f/STA but no wins on Good, and he has been running over 8-10f.

runners_data.name: Smoke Them Out
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse but mapped to midfield given the density of true closers; his best form has come on Heather ground (won twice on HEA) and he has only one placed effort in six Good-ground runs — the going is a meaningful downgrade.

runners_data.name: Summer Island
runners_data.note: A natural front-rank racer with Oisin Murphy booked — a high-profile jockey switch worth noting — but the prominent spots are congested and she may not secure her ideal position; her Good-ground sim record (1W2P from seven runs) is solid and she won over this course and distance last time.

runners_data.name: Thru And Thru
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator (tongue-tie) whose record on soft/heavy dominates his form; sim-going on Good shows 0W0P from seven runs, and with the map already compressed at the rear, he is effectively racing outside his comfort zone on both ground and position grounds.

runners_data.name: Una Matata
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner whose true position at the head of affairs is unlikely in this field given the logjam of similar types; his one Good-ground run (5/7f/GOO) was unplaced and his OR of 71 is the second-lowest in the race — connections are Adrian McGuinness (T14: 3/27) who has a live stable in the meeting.

runners_data.name: Apache Outlaw
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse (cheekpieces) but pushed into midfield on the map; he has been running frequently (LR 8d) and all of his recent form is at 5-6f on Standside or slow ground — 7f on Good turf is a significant ask and the form reads poorly for this test.

races.paceDynamic: Alfred Tennyson is the lone confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, critically, faces no credible pace rival to pressure him — he can dictate terms from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over seven furlongs. Behind him, a cluster of prominent types including Arryaaf, Indigo Dream, Spacebound, Collecting Coin, Little Empire and Spodo Komodo will contest the early positions immediately behind, creating a contested but not frenetic early pace. The hold-up contingent — Tolebi, Dar Toungi, Invincible Will, Um Wadi and others — will be last away but face a structurally sound pace to aim at. The field contains more prominent and hold-up types than can all settle naturally; Arryaaf, Indigo Dream and Collecting Coin are most likely to secure the front-rank positions behind Alfred Tennyson, while Summer Island, Una Matata and the redistributed hold-up horses (Smoke Them Out, Thru And Thru, Apache Outlaw) will be shuffled wider or deeper than their natural style. A controlled, single-file gallop that rewards horses who can sit just off the pace and sustain their run into the straight is the dominant shape — prominent hold-up types with a strong turn of foot at seven furlongs on Good ground are best positioned.

watchPoints.text: Alfred Tennyson controls the race from the front unchallenged — watch the early fractions; if Chris Hayes steals an unusually soft lead, the entire field may be chasing with too little time to close.

Invincible Will (OR 87, highest in the field) is Gavin Cromwell's yard's best recent performer and the most credentialled closer — watch where Jack Kearney positions him in the first two furlongs as a guide to whether this shape is truly a hold-up race or not.

With 18 runners over 7f, the transition from the straight run to the home bend creates a bottleneck — watch Summer Island and Collecting Coin for position at the two-furlong pole, as both are prominent types who could get caught in traffic if the field fans wide.

Arryaaf's 231-day absence means his fitness and early pace are unknowns — if he is sluggish away from the gate, the prominent positions fall to Indigo Dream and Collecting Coin and the race shape shifts meaningfully.

runners_data.name: Sea Eagle
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with Good-ground form at this sort of trip; 240-day absence is a concern, but jockey Danny O'Leary (7lb claim) is an asset and similar-going record of 8/15 shows competence; will be dropped out and needs gaps to open late in a large field.

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: Racing prominently out of true role — STYLE_FIT 0.91 — with only one placing from 15 runs on similar going; the sole confirmed pace-setter here, which means it has tactical control, but its weak recent form (204088) and low strike rate on Good ground make it a dubious leader rather than a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Pillar Of Hope
runners_data.note: Veteran of 8 at an age of 8 who reverts to 1m4f here; two recent top-4 finishes on similar ground suggest residual ability, but 18/10f effort on Good is a blot; McGettigan's 2lb claim helps marginally and he'll race prominently from a likely handy draw.

runners_data.name: Cracking Cloud
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4-year-old with three runs, trainer Ross O'Sullivan in good form at 2/15 over 14 days; Good-going form is encouraging (6th and 5th at 10f), stepping up in trip today and that extra distance should suit given his finishing style.

runners_data.name: Kool One
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on Good going not long ago and has placed repeatedly at this sort of trip; headgear note (tongue-tie), trainer Conor Maxwell modest in form, but the 7/14f Good run last time out is the one to focus on — a legitimate prominent-style contender at this distance.

runners_data.name: Granville Street
runners_data.note: Consistent older horse with three top-5 finishes over 13-14f on Good ground from his last six runs; headgear (hood/p) and 14-day break from a capable trainer; Ciaran Murphy at 2/16 is ticking over and Sam Coen's 2lb claim is a real asset in a 23-runner cavalry charge.

runners_data.name: Eastern Peace
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping up from shorter trips — all recent form is at 10f or less; third in latest run on Good ground is the best recent piece of form, but the trip question is genuine and 42 days off adds a layer of uncertainty here.

runners_data.name: Devine Genius
runners_data.note: 272-day layoff is a significant flag for a 2-year-old; hold-up style, and the form on Good ground (6/12f GOO) is modest; trainer Adrian Murray has one win from 18 over 14 days, making this look like a prep run.

runners_data.name: Derry Lad
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the map due to overcrowding at the rear; ⚠ finish-fade flag is the standout concern — 2-day turnaround is extremely quick for an 8-year-old, and 0 wins from 11 similar-going runs makes it hard to make a case despite the experience.

runners_data.name: Party Dress
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with a 249-day absence (92-day joint flag); two wins and four places from 15 on Good ground shows the ability exists, but the long absence and erratic recent form (29700-) means fitness is the primary question on return.

runners_data.name: Faro Island
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good going recently and has multiple placings on that surface; a true hold-up horse who has been redistributed to midfield on the map — in reality, likely to settle toward the rear; STYLE_FIT 0.92 means its chance depends on the race unfolding in a way that gives it a clean run.

runners_data.name: Celtic Druid
runners_data.note: Won twice at 12f on Standard, now encountering Good ground for the first time over 14f; the trip extension could help, but the 7lb claim for Sadhbh Tormey is novice-level and trainer T G McCourt is winless over 12 days; proximity on the RPR scale is the main argument.

runners_data.name: Tatum
runners_data.note: Won twice over 12-13f on Good going and has strong finishing form; nose-band headgear noted; trainer Noel Meade with one win from 18 over 14 days but the horse's own record — 2W5P in similar conditions — makes it one of the stronger prominent-style contenders in the race.

runners_data.name: Royal Alliance
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse relocated to midfield on the map — has yet to win and modest form figures (00-003) paint a limited picture; best effort (3rd at 13f SOF) came on soft, and the Good ground is the better surface for a horse that has struggled at 7-8f recently.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: Another genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to field congestion; 239-day absence is a real concern and the form (46442-) shows consistent placing without winning; Good-ground record of 3/15 is modest and the trainer has just one win from three recently.

runners_data.name: Keepsgettingbetter
runners_data.note: Strong candidate — three-year-old trained by Donnacha O'Brien, whose yard is in good nick at 3/11 over 14 days; won twice over shorter trips and third over 12f on Good going last time; stepup to 14f is the unknown but breeding/trainer combination suggests it will handle it.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Placed third on soft at 9f recently but all other form is modest; no jockey listed in data which is a minor concern; prominent style over a trip that appears beyond current form figures — modest claims.

runners_data.name: Darius Dark
runners_data.note: Two wins over 12f on Good ground give genuine claims; ⚠ fade flag tempers enthusiasm and trainer J P Murtagh at 3/32 over 14 days is a low strike rate; headgear (hood) worn throughout career; Rory Mulligan's 2lb claim is a positive if the horse can avoid its finishing drift.

runners_data.name: Nod Of Approval
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer trained by Mrs John Harrington, yard in strong form at 4/33 over 14 days; second over 12f on Good ground is the standout piece, but recent run of 2/12f was shorter than today's 14f — the trip extension is the key query.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Drills
runners_data.note: Unknown style (U) and only three career runs all at 10f; stepping up to 14f is a significant ask with no stamina evidence; trainer J S Bolger has one win from nine recently and Orla Tynan is a 7lb claimer — the apprentice Derby context is noted but the form is thin.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer who is likely to be forced off its preferred position in this large field — STYLE_FIT 0.93; Denis Hogan yard at 3/24 over 14 days, and the Good-going form over 12-13f (including multiple placings) shows ability, but racing further back than ideal will blunt its chance.

runners_data.name: Folly Beach
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 13f and 20f on similar ground; another naturally prominent horse who is likely to find itself racing in midfield due to the congested prominent positions — STYLE_FIT 0.92; no jockey listed and trainer M A Molloy has 0/2 recently, limiting confidence.

runners_data.name: Avoca Woods
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with only three runs and none at this trip; ⚠ fade flag and no wins or places on Good ground; trainer Jack Foley winless from five over 14 days — this looks like a learning experience over a trip significantly further than the horse has yet encountered.

races.paceDynamic: Quatre Bras is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 23-runner 1m4f handicap at the Curragh and, critically, is racing out of role — its STYLE_FIT tag of 0.91 signals this position is being taken more by default than natural aggression, meaning the pace it sets will be sustainable and unhurried rather than genuinely pressured. Behind it, a cluster of prominent types — Pillar Of Hope, Cracking Cloud, Kool One, Granville Street, Darius Dark, Celtic Druid, and Tatum — will all compete for the positions immediately behind the leader on good ground over a trip that rewards horses who can travel economically and finish strongly. The field contains significantly more prominent runners than the map can accommodate: Tassarolo and Folly Beach are natural prominent racers who are likely to be shuffled back into midfield, while Derry Lad, Faro Island, Royal Alliance, and Covert Legend are genuine hold-up horses similarly remapped toward midfield due to overcrowding at the rear. With one unhurried front-runner setting a controlled tempo on Good ground, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can travel in mid-to-rear and produce a sustained late run — particularly those with Good-ground form over 1m4f who are not compromised by their true position being squeezed out.

runners_data.name: Poetic Sound
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for G M Lyons and Colin Keane; won over 14f on Good recently and the step to 2m½f looks stretching, but the unchallenged lead is a significant advantage — STYLE_FIT tag is relevant only if things go wrong positionally, which is unlikely here as he simply goes forward.

runners_data.name: The Shunter
runners_data.note: Veteran of 11 years but fresh off a 236-day break — that layoff is the biggest concern; handles Good ground and has placed over 16f before, but this stamina test over 2m½f is searching and Emmet Mullins brings him back cold.

runners_data.name: Delta
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's 4yo wore a tongue-strap last time; Oisin Murphy booking is a significant upgrade and he sits a career-best OR of 92 — Good ground suits (5W/7P in sim-going), and tracking from a prominent position over this trip looks a natural fit.

runners_data.name: Kilmeaden
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's 4yo won over 16f on Heavy and placed twice over similar trips; Good ground slightly less proven but workable, and a prominent position under Paddy Harnett (5lb claim) gives him a tactical edge if things unfold smoothly.

runners_data.name: Reverend Hubert
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a remarkable record in similar conditions — four wins from 15 Good-ground runs and has triumphed over both 18f and 25f; the longest-distance runners in his history suggest he is the most likely beneficiary if the pace collapses, and trainer C Byrnes has been very quiet (0/11 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Too Bossy For Us
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' 5yo — no headgear — has a flat form profile with six placings but no wins over 14-16f on Good; DBM is an excellent booking but the consistent mid-table finishes make it hard to see where the winning improvement comes from at this trip.

runners_data.name: Highwind
runners_data.note: Second Mullins runner, a genuine hold-up type who has placed at 18f on Good; recent form (6-4-8-13-10) is patchy and a conversion from close placing to winning is required — Ben Coen retains the ride.

runners_data.name: Ballyadam
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 11yo veteran won over 16f on Good last time out (OR 83) and has been excellent in recent form (3-3-2-1); his natural prominent style means he will push forward regardless of mapping, so watch for him pressing for a realistic position in the first half-mile rather than settling in midfield.

runners_data.name: Robbies Rock
runners_data.note: A genuinely front-running type for Gavin Cromwell — 3 wins and 7 places on Good — whose most recent run (8th, 12f, Soft) was below form; the redistribution to midfield reflects the overcrowded pace positions, but he may push up early before tiring if the pace is quicker than anticipated.

runners_data.name: Happy Jacky
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old returning from 288 days (32 jumps starts in between), which makes him a major unknown quantity; his natural impulse is to race prominently, and that genuine front-running instinct means he could end up contributing to an unintended battle for position in the early stages.

runners_data.name: Cock And Bull
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse returning from 272 days off — the extended layoff (with 73 jumps runs intervening) is a serious fitness query; Good-ground form includes a win but recent finishes (11-7-5-8-9) suggest he will need to be at peak fitness to factor, which this comeback run makes uncertain.

runners_data.name: Hatim
runners_data.note: French-trained 4yo flagged for fading in the finish — that tendency is very damaging in a 2m½f slog; returning from 227 days off with only two UK/Irish runs on record, both on Soft, and the step to Good ground and this distance makes him extremely hard to assess positively.

runners_data.name: Carthusian
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's 4yo ran just 14 days ago and wears a hood; entirely unproven at this trip (career runs mostly 10-14f), and Good-ground form shows no wins; one of several natural front-runners whose true pace instincts will be frustrated here as the prominent slots are already taken.

races.paceDynamic: Poetic Sound is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a field of 13 over 2m½f on Good ground at the Curragh, Colin Keane can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — this is not a pressured pace scenario. Behind him, the field is unusually front-loaded: Ballyadam, Robbies Rock, Happy Jacky, and Carthusian are all natural prominent-racers who cannot all secure their preferred spot, meaning several will be shuffled back into unnatural midfield positions, likely creating a degree of shuffling and positional friction in the early stages. The Shunter, Delta, Kilmeaden, and Too Bossy For Us will also apply pressure from just off the pace, leaving a cluster of genuinely hold-up types — Reverend Hubert, Highwind, Cock And Bull — operating from the rear and needing the tempo to quicken late. With one genuine front-runner setting a measured gallop over this marathon trip on Good turf, the race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can travel prominently just behind Poetic Sound in the early stages and pounce at the top of the straight, with true hold-up horses needing more pace than this setup is likely to generate.

watchPoints.text: Poetic Sound's unchallenged lead is the pivotal variable — if Keane eases off in the early stages and sets a false pace, any horse travelling prominently directly behind him (Delta, Kilmeaden) could coast into a winning position before the field reacts.

Ballyadam, Robbies Rock, Happy Jacky and Carthusian are all natural front-runners who cannot all get to the front — watch the first two furlongs closely for positional jostling that could unsettle riders and burn energy in the horses most expected to travel prominently.

Reverend Hubert's trainer C Byrnes has a 0/11 record in the last 14 days, but the horse's own form at this trip and distance on Good ground is exceptional — he is a live danger if the pace shapes up for a hold-up horse, despite the trainer's current form.

Cock And Bull and Happy Jacky both return from very long absences (272 and 288 days) with significant jump-racing interruptions — treat their first-run-back fitness as genuinely unknown and be cautious about following any market support without confirmation of stable confidence.

Hatim is flagged as a fader and arrives from 227 days off having only raced on Soft ground — if he shows any early speed before tiring, he risks disrupting the rhythm of horses near him in the pack during the crucial middle section of this marathon trip.

runners_data.name: Spinola Bay
runners_data.note: Has a course-and-distance win on Good going in recent history and a Prominent style that fits this race shape perfectly; 157 days since last run is worth watching, but the 1W2P sim-going record and natural position close to Whatyouwant make her the standout tactical fit.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: Trainer Jack Foley sends this 7-year-old out 53 days after a Good-ground win at 23f — strong form on paper — but Catalani is a true prominent racer who is likely to be crowded out of that position in this traffic-heavy field and will need to perform from further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Red Hugh O'Donnell
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare dropping sharply back in distance to 1m4f from flat-course sprinting history, with a modest sim-going record of 0W1P across 9 attempts; the headgear note and trip make this a tough assignment regardless of pace shape.

runners_data.name: The Mediator
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends this consistent 9-year-old back 26 days after a placing, and the 1W5P record in similar going shows durability — but as a natural P-type forced to race in midfield by the congestion ahead, The Mediator will need gaps to open that may not come in a 16-runner field.

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Gillian Scott who has placed at big distances on Good and Soft, but the 27-day jumps absence and the fact she has no wins on Good ground in five attempts here (0W1P) moderates expectation even in a pace shape that suits her style.

runners_data.name: Banana Three
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's 4-year-old has a sensible 0W3P placed record on Good across recent runs, but with 716 days since a race and 394 since a jumps run, fitness is the primary question; naturally prominent but the congestion up front means Banana Three will find herself shuffled back, working against her best form position.

runners_data.name: Limbocall
runners_data.note: Style is listed as Unknown and the recent form string shows a 0 last time — this lightly-raced 4-year-old has been running at much shorter trips (8-9f) than today's 1m4f and the step up in distance combined with a 7-day turnaround makes this a very speculative entry.

runners_data.name: San Andreas
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's 10-year-old has placed twice at 1m4f on Standard surface but has no sim-going credit on turf Good (0W0P in 15 attempts), meaning his hold-up style needs a pace meltdown that is unlikely to arrive on this track and ground combination.

runners_data.name: Typical Thomas
runners_data.note: Long-absent 9-year-old (273 days, 13 days since a jumps run) whose 2W3P sim-going record on Good over staying trips is genuinely solid — the hold-up style means he needs the pace to stretch the field, and the layoff is a clear concern, but the trip suits if fitness is there.

runners_data.name: Wackestone
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's lightly-raced 4-year-old has a 0W0P record on Good in eight attempts but showed a placed effort at 1m4f previously — the 426-day absence and 81-day jumps gap is the dominant risk factor here, though the Prominent style would ideally suit this pace shape.

runners_data.name: Western Model
runners_data.note: Andrew Kinirons' 7-year-old holds a strong placed record over long distances on Good going (0W5P), suggesting he handles this surface well and stays, though 13 days since a jumps run and a tendency to finish runner-up rather than win raises a familiar concern.

runners_data.name: Nancee Spain
runners_data.note: The 4-year-old has winning form at 1m2f on Soft and placed on Good, with a natural hold-up style — she is redistributed into midfield because the rear is congested, which means she races in a role that doesn't fully suit, and her light weight (lowest in field at 166lbs) is a minor positive.

runners_data.name: Whatyouwant
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in this field who can dictate terms entirely — has winning form over similar trips on Good ground with a 2W2P sim-going record in 15 attempts, though 273 days absence (and 13-day jumps gap) and a STYLE_FIT tag reflecting the contested nature of a 16-runner field temper confidence despite the tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 5-year-old has a 1W3P record in Good-ground sim conditions and placed twice at 1m4f — the Prominent style suits perfectly here, and a 20-day jumps return is acceptable, though the OR=120 ceiling and a form string featuring a wide spread of finishes (1 to 9) suggests inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Elman
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's 4-year-old hold-up horse has an unresolved form record at 1m6f on Soft and Heavy, with no confirmed finishing positions available; the 87-day jumps gap and sparse form evidence make this a very difficult runner to assess positively.

runners_data.name: Garnetot
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 5-year-old stays well and has a placed effort at 2m on Good in recent history, with headgear flagged — as a genuine hold-up type with a 0W1P sim-going record he needs the front end to stop, which the controlled Whatyouwant-led pace makes unlikely, though 13 days since a jumps run suggests Elliott has him ready.

races.paceDynamic: Whatyouwant is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner 1m4f charity race at the Curragh and, critically, is uncontested — no other genuine lead horse lines up to push the pace from the front. With Good ground confirmed throughout the card and a clean rail to exploit, Whatyouwant can dictate a controlled, even tempo from the outset, likely setting fractions that suit horses travelling prominently behind rather than those buried deep in the field. The pack behind is crowded with prominent-types — Spinola Bay, Way Down South, Wackestone, Western Model, and Playtime are all natural P-style horses who will press forward and fill the positions immediately behind the leader, creating a compact, organised front end. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate in those forward berths — Catalani, Banana Three, and The Mediator are natural prominent racers who are unlikely to secure their preferred position and will be shuffled back into a midfield role they do not relish. The tactical verdict is clear: a single uncontested pace-setter setting a sustainable rhythm on Good ground strongly favours prominent-held horses who can travel close to the leader throughout and strike in the straight without having to find an extra gear from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Whatyouwant's 273-day absence is the single biggest danger to the entire pace map — if fitness fails and the horse is outpaced early or fades before the straight, the race loses its pace anchor and shape becomes unpredictable for all 16 runners.

Monitor the first two furlongs for Catalani, Banana Three, and The Mediator all attempting to press forward simultaneously — if even one of them succeeds in holding a prominent position it pressures Whatyouwant and converts the controlled gallop into a genuinely contentious early pace.

Spinola Bay's 157-day absence for Gordon Elliott means she arrives fit-on-paper but race-sharpness is unproven; if she fails to fire from her natural prominent position, the horses best placed to capitalise are the other prominent types rather than closers.

Western Model and Way Down South have both placed multiple times in similar conditions but have not broken through to win — watch whether either can convert a tactically ideal position (tracking Whatyouwant) into a first win, or whether this profile repeats the placed habit.

Garnetot carries headgear and returns just 13 days after a jumps run for Gordon Elliott — the trainer's strong 11/49 T14 record is worth noting, and Elliott has four runners in this race (Spinola Bay, The Mediator, Wackestone, Playtime, Garnetot), creating potential pace management considerations across the yard's string.
